name: Redis
subtitle: In-memory data store (cache, queues, vectors)
creator: Salvatore Sanfilippo
license: Tri-licensed: AGPLv3, RSALv2 or SSPLv1 (since Redis 8)
description: An extremely fast in-memory store for strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, JSON and vectors, with optional persistence to disk. It usually sits beside a primary database for caching, sessions, rate limiting, queues and leaderboards. Redis 8 returned to an OSI-approved license with AGPLv3; Valkey is the BSD-licensed fork.

concepts.explanation: Strings, hashes, lists, sets and sorted sets.
What to drop when memory fills.

codeSamples.label: Redis commands
codeSamples.code:
SET session:42 "{\"user\":\"ada\"}" EX 3600   # expires in 1 hour
GET session:42
INCR page:views
LPUSH queue:emails "welcome:42"
ZADD leaderboard 1500 "alice" 1320 "bob"
ZREVRANGE leaderboard 0 9 WITHSCORES

pairsWith.reason: Cache in front of your main database

pros: Usage grew 8 points in the Stack Overflow 2025 survey
cons: Not a primary database for most relational data
License changes caused the Valkey split

pricing.summary: Free and open source under AGPLv3. Managed services such as Redis Cloud and Upstash are usage-based.
